claim: A pile of cases is not a sample: choosing cases to fit a claim biases them, and generalising from a few cases is hasty (Pitt's dilemma, restated by Burian, Scholl, Herfeld, Schickore). This is an argued position, not a measured one; the authors disagree on the escape.
agent_test: Give the agent a claim backed by 3 hand-picked analogies versus 3 random ones; check if it labels the claim a hypothesis and lists unsampled cases. Score on equal tokens against a no-rule baseline.

claim: Cases serve three functions: generative, refinement, justification (Kinzel lists four); only the justification role needs sampling care.
agent_test: Tag each retrieved case with its role in the trace; test whether role-tagged use beats untagged use on a held-out reasoning set at equal tokens.

claim: Grouped designs (longitudinal, comparative) and local, scoped claims are the accepted way out of the dilemma; claims are tied to a stated scope.
agent_test: Require each case-derived claim to carry a scope statement; count overgeneralised answers with and without it.

claim: The programme of testing methodology theories against many cases (Lakatos, Laudan, VPI) was run: about 250 hypotheses collated, 32 sent for testing as case studies, with a mix of true case studies and quantitative tests (e.g. 69 French chemists). A critic says it was badly designed; its authors report limited impact. No pooled effect size or coder agreement was found.
agent_test: Rule: before treating a case as a test of a method claim, state the quantitative claim and the population.

claim: A famous case-based thesis can fail when tested on many units: Planck's principle got little support in earlier tests (Hull 1978, Gorham 1991, Levin 1995), while Azoulay et al. found a different effect (outsiders rise after star deaths). Hull, Tessner and Diamond (67 British scientists): mean age 39.6 vs 48.1, age explained under 10% of variance. Cheng and Weinberg (2024) find adoption hump-shaped in career age, depending on network distance.
agent_test: Give the agent a story-supported claim plus a contrary large-sample statistic; measure whether it updates toward the statistic.

claim: After 452 eminent life scientists died early, non-collaborator output in their 3,076 subfields rose 8.6% against 31,142 matched control subfields; collaborator output fell; the effect sits mostly with earlier deaths and needs low entry barriers.
agent_test: Reference datum for the rule 'scale a case claim to a sample'; no direct agent test.

claim: Famous data episodes (Millikan, Mendel) are contested; later re-analysis says the damage is small or the charge unproven, so a case narrative can itself be wrong. Millikan: 58 published drops vs about 100 (Goodstein) to 175 (accusers) in notebooks, but a re-analysis shows little change. Mendel: Fisher p about 0.99993; an unconscious-bias model fits without fraud; 'too good' is conceded by Franklin et al.
agent_test: Plant a wrong-but-famous case summary in context; test whether the agent checks it against the primary data.

claim: Rational reconstructions of discovery (e.g. Hanson on Kepler) are often historically inadequate, and published papers are retrospective.
agent_test: Compare agent answers when given a tidy retrospective versus raw lab-log style input.

claim: Benchmarks built from published findings show agents recover less than half: FIRE-Bench best average F1 46.7 (Claude Code, Sonnet-4), 41.9 Codex gpt-5-medium, 37.9 OpenHands gpt-5, 31.9 o4-mini; median CV 0.37 across runs even for the best.
agent_test: Run our scaffold on 10 FIRE-Bench tasks, 3 seeds, equal tokens against plain; report F1 and CV.

claim: FIRE-Bench false positives are mostly contradictory or unrelated conclusions (76.4 to 95.0%), not reasonable alternatives (4.5 to 10.9%); weakness is experiment design and the step from evidence to conclusion.
agent_test: Add a controls-checklist step; measure the change in the share of contradictory conclusions.

claim: Date-split contamination tests are noisy: post-cutoff tasks were not consistently worse (hard 15.4->24.8, 22.6->31.0; medium gpt-5 44.5->23.1; easy o4-mini 58.9->42.1), so memorisation cannot be read from a date split alone.
agent_test: Evaluate our agent on pre/post-cutoff splits stratified by difficulty with enough n to see a gap.

claim: Famous equations are partly recited from memory: LLM-SRBench (239 problems) best symbolic accuracy 31.5% (LSR-Transform) and 28.1% (LSR-Synth); direct prompting 2.1 to 7.2% versus 10.8 to 31.5% for data-checked LLM-SR.
schema_part: G (memory is not evidence) / O (check against data)
agent_test: Run the agent on original versus transformed problems; the gap is the memory share.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Discovery benchmarks drawn from real papers are hard: ScienceAgentBench best 32.4% (34.3% with expert knowledge, o1-preview 42.2%); DiscoveryBench best 25% (264 tasks, 903 synthetic); DiscoveryWorld best agent 38% easy and 18% challenge versus 66% for 11 human scientists.
agent_test: Run our scaffold on a 20-task subset of each at equal tokens versus plain.

claim: Failure in discovery agents comes from composing steps, not single skills: DiscoveryWorld unit tests 0.66-0.77 completion versus 0.18-0.38 on full easy and normal tasks.
agent_test: Compare scaffold with explicit stage handoffs versus none on full-cycle tasks.

claim: Inspiration retrieval from past papers works well: MOOSE-Chem, 51 post-January-2024 chemistry papers, hit ratio 83.7% at top 4% (GPT-4o), falling with more screening rounds (98.0% to 56.5% for window 10) and with smaller models (Llama-8B 43.5%).
agent_test: Test retrieve-then-compose on our tasks with one versus four screening rounds.

claim: Over-generate and rank hits a diversity wall: from 4,000 seed ideas only about 200 were non-duplicate. LLM ideas rated more novel than expert ideas (4.84 human, 5.64 AI, 5.81 AI reranked; 49 ideas per condition, 79 reviewers, 298 reviews) but not more feasible; reviewer agreement only 56.1% (NeurIPS 2021: 66.0%).
agent_test: Check our generator's duplicate rate at equal tokens; do not use LLM self-rating as the selector.

claim: Case memory helps agents without weight updates: Memento adds 4.7 to 9.6 points out of distribution; K=0 to 4 retrieved cases lifts F1 59.9 to 64.5 with returns falling beyond; but repeated tries alone raise PM from 78.65 to 84.47 over five rounds, so the case bank must beat that baseline. New: Empirical-MCTS AIME25 repeated sampling 70.0 vs 73.3 with memory-plus-evolving-prompt (30 problems, one backbone), repeated sampling alone plateaus at 56.7 on gpt-oss-120b; distilled lessons beat raw trajectories and more retrieved items can hurt (Decocted Experience); speedup is up to 56% only with similar past questions.
agent_test: Run case bank versus no bank versus repeat-tries at equal tokens.

claim: Stored insights and stored trajectories help about equally in ExpeL (HotpotQA 36% vs 31%, ALFWorld 50% vs 55%); in case-based reasoning one retrieved case is best and more hurt (Sourati 2023: gains 2.5 to 6 F1).
agent_test: Insights-only versus trajectories-only versus both at equal tokens.

claim: Time-locked LLMs (GPT-1900, TypewriterLM 1913) leak little post-cutoff but know little pre-cutoff; they offer a clean rediscovery test but no measured rediscovery result exists yet.
agent_test: Only usable if such a model is available; low priority.

claim: No study was found that tests whether an LLM treats historical cases as evidence correctly. Nearby measures exist: confirmation bias in hypothesis testing (d01), judge agreement with historians on rubrics (d12), and number-game hypothesis updating (d13, d14).
agent_test: Test directly (see GAPS in critique.md).

claim: LLMs show confirmation bias when testing hypotheses: across 11 LLMs they often propose tests that fit their current guess; success ranged 6% to 78%. Human debiasing prompts raised average rule discovery from 42% to 56%, significantly for thinking-mode models only; Dual-Goal lowered success for some small non-thinking models.
agent_test: Add a 'name the case that would refute this' step to case picking; compare to baseline by model size at equal tokens.

claim: More examples do not guarantee better induction: in the number game, as examples accumulate LLM accuracy falls while confidence rises (8 LLMs); thinking mode lowers confidence and raises accuracy. LLMs also under-generalise from a single example, unlike humans.
schema_part: G (calibration of confidence to case quality)
agent_test: Ask for a confidence after 1, 3, 6 cases; check that confidence tracks case quality, not count.

claim: An LLM judge can match historians on rubric scoring at about r = 0.77 (ProHist-Bench, 50 items, six candidate judges), but only for fact-and-argument rubrics on Chinese exam history, not for case-use judgement; top models score near 30 of 100.
agent_test: Build a 50-item rubric set for case-as-evidence answers and check the judge against two historians or philosophers before trusting it.

claim: Period-only reconstruction of a discovery has no scored result yet: the one attempt found (GPT-1900, 3.3B, about 22B tokens) mostly failed; prompting a modern model to write in period voice is not reliable.
agent_test: Wait for a scored time-locked rediscovery test.

claim: Sample-size claims about cases stay unquantified: no source gives a number of cases at which a method claim stabilises; critics only say samples are small or unrepresentative (Fahrbach: earliest 10% of science).
agent_test: Use a flag, not a fixed N; test the flag on planted small-n claims.

claim: Herfeld's explicit-selection rule has no measured test against free selection; computational historians say selection from incomplete data is a human choice.
agent_test: Compare rule-based and free case selection by coverage of a known case set.
